latin: Quinti, si tibi vis oculos debere Catullum
english: Quintius, if you want Catullus to owe you his eyes
suggested: Quintius, if you want Catullus to owe you [his] eyes

english: to say, and insidias, Arrius, hinsidias,
problem: Commas around Arrius make the nominative subject read as a vocative address.
suggested: to say, and insidias Arrius [said] hinsidias,

latin: quid facit is patruum qui non sinit esse maritum?
english: What does he do who does not allow his uncle to be a husband?
suggested: What does he do who does not allow [his] uncle to be a husband?

latin: non si demisso se ipse voret capite.
english: not if, his head bent down, he himself should devour himself.
suggested: not if, [his] head bent down, he himself should devour himself.

latin: Nascatur magus ex Gelli matrisque nefando
english: Let a magus be born from Gellius' and his mother's unspeakable
problem: Possessive 'his' (mother's) supplied without a note; Latin is simply 'of Gellius and of the mother'.
suggested: Let a magus be born from Gellius' and [his] mother's unspeakable

latin: aut posse a turpi mentem inhibere probro,
english: or able from base disgrace to restrain your mind,
suggested: or able from base disgrace to restrain [your] mind,

latin: culpa est in quacumque est aliquid sceleris.
english: fault in which there is anything of crime.
suggested: fault in whichever there is anything of crime.

english: drops you wiped with all your finger-joints,
suggested: drops you wiped with all [your] finger-joints,

latin: ut mi ex ambrosia mutatum iam fores illud
english: so that for me, changed from ambrosia, now was that
problem: The source prints fores (2nd sg.), which cannot agree with illud; the English correctly renders foret, but the note wrongly glosses fores = esses (2nd person) instead of flagging the source misprint for foret.
suggested: so that for me, changed from ambrosia, now was that  [note: fores: source misprint for foret (= esset)]

latin: tu, quod promisti mihi, quod mentita, inimica es;
english: You, because what you promised me, because you lied, are hostile;
problem: 'because what you promised me' adds 'what' and mixes a relative reading into the causal quod ... quod parallel.
suggested: You, because you promised me, because you lied, are hostile;

english: Aufilena, to live content with one husband alone
suggested: Aufilena, to live content with husband alone

latin: fertur, qui tot res in se habet egregias,
english: is said to be, who has in it so many outstanding things,
problem: qui with reflexive in se must refer to the estate (saltus), as the writer's own note says, so 'who ... in it' wrongly makes Mentula the antecedent and breaks the reflexive.
suggested: is said to be, which has in itself so many outstanding things,

english: In vain: the yield with his expenses he exceeds.
suggested: In vain: the yield by [his] expenses he exceeds.

latin: quare concedo sit dives, dum omnia desint;
english: Therefore I grant he is rich, provided all things are lacking;
problem: sit is subjunctive (concessive 'let him be rich'); 'he is rich' flattens the mood.
suggested: Therefore I grant he be rich, provided all things are lacking;

latin: tela infesta mihi mittere in usque caput,
english: hostile weapons to send at me even up to my head,
suggested: hostile weapons to send at me even up to [my] head,

latin: contra nos tela ista tua evitamus amictu:
english: Against them, those weapons of yours we avoid with a cloak:
problem: contra is adverbial ('in turn', as the writer's own note says) and nos is the subject; 'Against them' adds 'them' and turns contra into a preposition.
suggested: In turn we those weapons of yours avoid with a cloak:
